project.name: circulant-krr-climate
project.topic: Exact kernel ridge regression on regular-grid climate fields via block-circulant structure exploitation and the FFT
project.description: Research project with the primary research question being an ALGORITHMIC / METHODOLOGICAL innovation in machine learning: making exact kernel ridge regression (and GP-style predictive uncertainty) tractable on regular latitude/longitude climate grids under consumer hardware by exploiting the block-circulant structure of stationary kernels with FFT-based solves (O(N log N) training, O(N) memory, no N-by-N kernel matrix). AI-for-climate is the experimental substrate: sea-surface temperature anomaly fields for field reconstruction/gap-filling and ENSO (Nino3.4 index) regression. Compared against scikit-learn baselines: exact KRR (subsampled), Nystrom approximation, and Random Fourier Features. Deliverable: a compiled 4-page PDF (4 pages main text excluding references) in NeurIPS-workshop LaTeX formatting compiled with tectonic, written as an ML methods paper with climate-domain experiments.

boundaries: PRIMARY research question is algorithmic/methodological: exact kernel ridge regression on regular-grid climate fields via block-circulant structure + FFT (training and prediction in O(N log N), memory O(N), no explicit NxN kernel matrix); the climate domain is the experimental substrate, not the claimed contribution

Methodological claims: (1) the circulant-block algorithm and its CPU-only NumPy/SciPy implementation; (2) honest resource accounting (wall-clock, peak RSS, flop/memory scaling) as first-class result axes; (3) accuracy-per-flop and accuracy-per-byte comparison against scikit-learn baselines: exact KRR on subsamples, Nystrom, Random Fourier Features; (4) honest block/leave-one-field-out cross-validation (no random point splits leaking spatial/temporal autocorrelation), calibration of predictive intervals, and applicability analysis

Experimental substrate: publicly available sea-surface temperature (SST) anomaly fields (open NOAA-family source if fetchable; otherwise bundled/synthetic-from-physics fallback WITH explicit simulation markers in every artifact and the paper); tasks: masked-field reconstruction (gap-filling) and Nino3.4 (ENSO) index regression
All quantitative results come from our own CPU-only runs; every number in the paper traces to an artifact JSON produced by the analysis code; data/model/container claims match artifacts exactly

Honest positioning: spectral/FFT kernel techniques exist in the literature; the contribution is the concrete circulant-block algorithm for grid fields, its consumer-hardware implementation, and the first systematic CPU-only benchmark of exact-vs-randomized kernel methods on climate fields under memory constraints

Deliverable is a compiled 4-page PDF: 4 pages of main text excluding references, NeurIPS-workshop LaTeX style compiled with tectonic (verified on this host); structure: abstract, introduction, related work, methods, experiments/results, discussion/limitations, references

Iteration 2 (research-manager directive, 2026-08-31): real data utilisation is permitted -- reading real netCDF-4/HDF5 climate data via h5py (installed via apt) is allowed; all other boundaries (CPU-only, ~12 cores, ~7 GB, <=90 min, honest claims, no FFT-kernel newness claim) unchanged

constraints: CPU-only: no GPU or accelerator hardware; ~12 cores, ~7 GB RAM available
Python scientific stack limited to what is installed: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib (no pandas/statsmodels/torch; stdlib otherwise)
Total wall-clock compute budget for all experiment runs: <= 90 minutes on this machine
All datasets publicly available and < 2 GB total on disk; if network fetch fails, fall back to bundled/synthetic-from-physics data ONLY with explicit simulation markers in all artifacts and the paper
Analysis code must run end-to-end via a single script or Makefile target and be committed to the project workspace repo
